issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Rideable.messageOnRide() with no parameters (returns a String), and the template Main expects to call messageOnRide() without arguments. However, the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and the implementations (Pig, Seal) require an int parameter. This method-parameter mismatch means students following the problem/template will implement a parameterless method, but the solution/tests use a version with a parameter (and vice versa), causing compilation/test incompatibilities and confusion about the intended interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution repository's Rideable and its implementations (Pig, Seal) to declare and implement messageOnRide() with no parameters (returning the expected String), so it matches the UML/problem statement and the template Main. Alternatively, if the speed parameter is intentional, update the problem statement, UML, and template Main to specify messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust examples accordingly.

issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method is specified in the problem statement and used in the template as a no-argument method returning a string like "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (and implementations in Pig and Seal accept an int and include speed in the returned message). This signature/name mismatch across artifacts prevents students from mapping the requirement to the implementation and will cause compilation/runtime discrepancies with the provided template code and expected behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface and all its implementations consistent with the problem/template by using the no-argument signature messageOnRide() that returns "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Concretely, change solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Rideable.java to declare String messageOnRide(); and update Pig.java and Seal.java to implement messageOnRide() (no parameters) returning the expected string format. Alternatively, if the speed parameter is desired, update the problem statement and template calls to require and use messageOnRide(int speed) consistently.
